text:
Alex: Heads-up — we're seeing a bunch of GPU jobs stuck Pending in us-west-2. Pods request nodeSelector: redwood.com/gpu=true but they never schedule and CA (cluster-autoscaler) doesn't scale the GPU nodepool. Anyone seen this pattern?
Maya: Ugh. Do the pending pods have tolerations for the GPU taint? Our GPU nodepools are tainted with redwood.com/gpu=true:NoSchedule.
Alex: I checked one pod quick: no tolerations. We added the taint ages ago to keep CPU workloads off GPUs. Thought CA would still spin up nodes that are tainted though?
Sam: CA will scale up if it can find a nodegroup that would fit the pod. But if the pod requires label/affinity that CA can't match to a nodegroup the autoscaler knows about, it won't. Also if new nodes always come tainted and pod lacks toleration, scheduler still can't bind. Two separate gaps: label matching AND toleration.
Maya: Exactly. For GPU pools we need both: nodeSelector/nodeAffinity to pick the GPU pool and a toleration for the taint. Otherwise scheduler rejects and CA may report "no nodes fit" and not trigger scale up.
Alex: Here's the debug commands I ran: 
```
kubectl describe pod gpu-job-67
kubectl get nodepool -l redwood.com/pool=gpu -o wide
kubectl logs -n kube-system cluster-autoscaler
```
infra-bot: [autoscaler] event: Pod gpu-job-67 unschedulable: 0/10 nodes are available: 10 taints match.
Zach: That autoscaler message means it saw the reason "taints match" which usually indicates pod didn't tolerate the taint. CA should still attempt scale-up if there is a nodegroup with matching labels to host the pod. If your GPU nodegroup has label redwood.com/gpu=true then CA must be configured to consider that nodegroup.
Priya: FYI we have two GPU pools in us-west-2: gpu-on-demand (no preemptible, tainted redwood.com/gpu=true) and gpu-spot (tainted redwood.com/gpu=true, preemptible=true). CA config uses expander: priority and has both groups. But our pod spec only had `nodeSelector: {redwood.com/gpu: "true"}` and no tolerations.
Maya: Quick patch suggestion — add this toleration + nodeAffinity to the pod template: 
```
tolerations:
  - key: "redwood.com/gpu"
    operator: "Equal"
    value: "true"
    effect: "NoSchedule"
nodeAffinity:
  requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
    nodeSelectorTerms:
      - matchExpressions:
          - key: "redwood.com/gpu"
            operator: In
            values: ["true"]
```
Sam: Also confirm that the nodegroup's autoscaler tags are correct (so CA knows it's a candidate): for eks/gke that means the nodegroup name or provider IDs are exposed. On AWS/eks ensure the ASG has the cluster-autoscaler node label annotation.
Alex: I added the toleration + nodeAffinity to the helm chart and triggered a redeploy of the job pods. They started to scale after ~45s and CA spun up a gpu-spot nodegroup.
Priya: Note — we saw an intermittent race where CA selected gpu-spot but the spot instance was slow to register, scheduler kept failing and the pod restarted repeatedly. To reduce churn, I set pod disruption and backoff as: `spec.backoffLimit: 4` and added `schedulerName: default-scheduler` (no fancy sched plugin).
Zach: Longer-term I'd recommend:
- Make GPU pod templates include both toleration and explicit nodeAffinity.
- Avoid using only nodeSelector as it's less expressive for multi-arch pools.
- Add a small startup probe so pods don't rapidly fail on node registration delays.
- Consider using the cluster-autoscaler flag `--scale-up-from-zero=true` if you have nodegroups that can start from zero.
Maya: Another cost/ops note: tainting both on-demand and spot GPU groups means you must ensure tolerations don't accidentally let CPU batch jobs land on expensive GPUs. Use separate labels for "gpu-type=on-demand|spot" and set affinity accordingly.
Alex: Good call. I'm going to add `redwood.com/gpu-type=spot` label and require it for non-critical jobs. Critical (SLA) training should target on-demand pool via affinity/kubernetes nodeSelector.
Sam: One more gotcha: if you use tolerations with operator Exists, it can be too permissive. Prefer `key=..., operator=Equal, value=true` so only pods that explicitly opt-in tolerate GPUs.
Priya: Patch merged to staging. I'll watch CA logs for 30m and escalate if flapping continues. Thanks all :thumbsup:
Alex: Status update — resolved for now. Will follow up with a short runbook so engineers know the expected pod spec for GPU workloads.
